# QS-CFW-5798-88 Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (4340)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-5798-88

Scope
This quality specification applies to the manufacture, inspection, and disposition of crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (4340) produced at Plant P2. It defines critical acceptance criteria, the prescribed inspection methods, and the nonconformance handling process for material and dimensional requirements specific to the crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88. This document is mandatory for production, first article, incoming material verification, and final inspection activities associated with part CFW-5798-88.

Background and rationale
Crankshaft blanks are safety and performance critical forgings. Control of hardness, bore geometry, and weight is essential to ensure downstream machinability, heat treat response, and handling during machining and assembly. The criteria in this specification reflect metallurgical and process capability limits derived from engineering design and forging process constraints. Inspecting these features at the blank stage prevents costly scrap and rework later in the manufacturing flow.

Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Material identification | Must be 4340 forging for CFW-5798-88 | Traceable material certification required | Certification must reference part CFW-5798-88 |
| Hardness | Hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) | 25-29 HRC | Hardness measured as specified in inspection method |
| Bore diameter | Bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) | ±0.09 mm | Applies to all machined bore features on blank |
| Forging weight | Maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) | 119.4 kg | Weigh each forging and record value |

Inspection method
General
All inspections shall be performed by trained personnel using calibrated equipment. Calibration records must be current and traceable to national or internal standards. Reference the plant calibration control process for detailed calibration intervals and methods.

Hardness measurement
Select a representative sample from each production lot for hardness testing. Hardness shall be measured using appropriate Rockwell C scale methodology and indenter type consistent with the hardness range in the requirements table. Take readings on the forging surface areas designated for raw blank hardness checks, avoiding quenched or distorted zones. Record individual readings and compute lot disposition based on the range requirement Hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is 25-29 HRC. If hardness readings vary within the lot, follow the nonconformance handling steps.

Bore diameter measurement
Inspect bore geometry using a bore gauge or coordinate measurement method appropriate for blind and through bores on the blank. The acceptance criterion is Bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is ±0.09 mm. Measure at defined locations along the bore axis to identify taper and out-of-round conditions. Record nominal diameter and deviation from nominal for each measured bore feature. For example, record the measured value and the deviation relative to nominal, and mark parts that exceed the permitted deviation for segregation.

Weight verification
Weigh each finished forging on a calibrated industrial scale. Compare the measured mass to Maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is 119.4 kg. Forgings that exceed the maximum forging weight shall be segregated and placed into nonconforming disposition until reviewed by engineering. Record the as-weighed mass and operator initials on the inspection record.

Sampling and lot disposition
Apply sampling where lot quantities are produced by a single heat and die set. Use inspection sampling practices consistent with plant quality procedures. If any sampled item fails to meet the requirements table criteria, escalate to full lot inspection. Document all inspection data in the quality record for the lot.

Nonconformance handling
Identification and segregation
Any crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 that does not meet the requirements in the requirements table shall be immediately identified and segregated from acceptable inventory. Mark nonconforming material clearly and apply a nonconformance tag referencing this document and the inspection record.

Containment and evaluation
Containment actions shall prevent inadvertent use of nonconforming crankshaft blanks. The lot or individual pieces shall be evaluated by quality engineering in coordination with production and metallurgical engineering. Evaluation shall determine whether rework, reheat, documentation waiver, or scrap is appropriate. Examples of evaluation outcomes include metallurgical investigation for hardness out of range, dimensional analysis for bore deviations, and mass reconciliation for weight excess.

Disposition
Dispositions may include rework, reheat and re-inspect, use-as-is with documented engineering waiver, or scrap. Engineering waivers shall be documented with justification, risk assessment, and end item impact statement. Waivers require approval by authorized engineering personnel. Any rework or reprocessing must be performed under controlled instructions and re-inspected using the inspection method above to confirm conformance to the requirements table.

Records to keep
Retain the following records with lot traceability:
- Material certification linking heat lot to part CFW-5798-88.
- Hardness test records showing individual readings and lot summary demonstrating compliance with Hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is 25-29 HRC.
- Bore measurement records listing measured values and deviations demonstrating compliance with Bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is ±0.09 mm.
- Weighing records showing measured mass and confirmation of Maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-5798-88 (CFW-5798-88) is 119.4 kg.
- Nonconformance reports, containment evidence, engineering evaluations, and final dispositions.

Audit and review
Quality shall periodically review inspection records for trends indicating process drift. Findings that indicate recurring nonconformance shall trigger corrective action and process improvement activities in accordance with Plant P2 quality procedures.

End of document.
